grammar_concept.title: Nominalisation
grammar_concept.rule: Turn verbs and adjectives into nouns (nominalisation) to create a more formal, dense, 'academic' style, common in reports, essays and news — 'decide' becomes 'decision', 'analyse' becomes 'analysis', 'available' becomes 'availability'.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Formal English often prefers a noun + a general verb (make a decision, conduct an analysis, reach a conclusion) over the plain verb (decide, analyse, conclude). This isn't just style for its own sake — it's the expected register in reports, essays and news writing.
grammar_concept.example: We need to make a decision. (formal, nominalised) vs. We need to decide. (plain verb) — The analysis of the data revealed a clear pattern.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Precisamos de tomar uma decisão. vs. Precisamos de decidir. — A análise dos dados revelou um padrão claro.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: O português também nominaliza, mas ao escrever em inglês formal os alunos tendem a manter sempre a estrutura mais simples com verbo ("We need to decide") mesmo quando o registo pede o substantivo ("make a decision"), ou tentam criar formas nominais erradas por analogia direta ("the decide" em vez de "the decision").
grammar_concept.correction: Em registo formal/académico, prefira o substantivo derivado + um verbo genérico (make/reach/come to a decision, conduct an analysis) em vez do verbo direto — mas aprenda a forma nominal certa de cada verbo, porque muitas são irregulares (decide → decision, analyse → analysis, know → knowledge).
grammar_concept.real_world_example: In a report: "The team conducted a thorough analysis before reaching a final decision."

vocabulary.definition_en: to organize and carry out a particular activity, such as research or an analysis
example_sentences: The team conducted a thorough analysis of the results.

vocabulary.definition_en: detailed examination of something in order to understand it
example_sentences: The analysis revealed a clear pattern.

vocabulary.definition_en: the state of being able to be used or obtained
example_sentences: Please confirm your availability for next week.

exercises.prompt: Choose the more formal version: "The board needs to ___ before Friday."
exercises.explanation: "Make a decision" é a forma nominalizada formal de "decide".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Inventar formas como "decide-ment" por analogia é comum ao tentar nominalizar verbos irregulares.

exercises.prompt: Choose the more formal version: "We need to ___ of the data before proceeding."
exercises.explanation: A forma nominal correta de "analyse" é "analysis", combinada com o verbo genérico "conduct": "conduct an analysis".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "analyse" como substantivo ("do an analyse") é o erro mais comum aqui.

exercises.prompt: What is the noun form of "available"?
exercises.explanation: A forma nominal correta é "availability", não uma forma inventada por analogia direta.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What did the team do before reaching a decision?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "The team conducted a thorough analysis before reaching a final decision."
exercises.transcript: The team conducted a thorough analysis of all the available data before reaching a final decision on the new strategy.

exercises.prompt: Read: "Please confirm your availability for a meeting next Tuesday." What is being requested?
correct_answer: confirmation of availability for a meeting
whether the person is free next Tuesday
exercises.explanation: O texto pede a confirmação da disponibilidade para uma reunião.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English (usando a forma nominalizada, mais formal): "A equipa vai realizar uma análise completa dos resultados."
correct_answer: The team will conduct a thorough analysis of the results.
exercises.explanation: "Realizar uma análise" corresponde a "conduct an analysis", a forma nominalizada e formal, em vez de "analyse the results" (verbo direto).
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir apenas com o verbo ("The team will analyse the results") não está errado, mas não é a forma nominalizada formal pedida.

steps.content: Nominalised words often shift their stress compared to the verb they come from: DEcide → deCIsion, aNAlyse → aNAlysis stays similar, but many nominalisations move stress toward the new suffix (-tion, -sion, -ity) — listen for the syllable that changes.

steps.prompt: Describe a decision you made recently using formal nominalised language ('I made a decision to...', 'After conducting an analysis of...').
Write 3 formal sentences using nominalisation instead of the plain verb (e.g. 'make a decision' instead of 'decide').
